prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1240; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just be identified as the claimant on this one, if that's okay.
Q: That's acceptable. Can you describe where you were when the collision occurred?
A: I was driving in Katy, Texas, on a two-lane road heading toward the shopping center. It was a weekday afternoon and traffic was moving slowly.
Q: What happened right before the impact?
A: The vehicle in front of me on the other side stopped suddenly. Then the other car drifted into my lane. I braked, but we still ended up making contact nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, more like a jolt.
Q: What speed do you estimate you were traveling?
A: Maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour. I was barely moving.
Q: Did either airbag deploy?
A: No, nothing deployed. Both cars drove away from the scene under their own power, though the other driver's bumper was hanging down a bit.
Q: Tell me about your injuries.
A: My right shoulder started hurting almost immediately. I felt a sharp pain when I turned the wheel, and by the next morning it was stiff and I couldn't lift my arm above my head comfortably.
Q: Have you seen a doctor?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care that evening and I've scheduled a follow-up with my regular physician. They mentioned possible strain and I may need physical therapy.
Q: Did you have any shoulder problems before this collision?
A: I had some minor soreness from lifting boxes at work a while back, but nothing that kept me from my normal activities.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I want to make sure my medical bills and time off work are considered. I'm still getting evaluated.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
